questions.q: What is the standard two-line pattern for loading a model from the Hugging Face Hub?
options: AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(name) and AutoModel.from_pretrained(name), both given the same model name
A single call to pipeline() with no arguments
Manually downloading a .zip file from the Hub's website
AutoModel.train(name) followed by AutoModel.save(name)
questions.explain: Both the tokenizer and the model are loaded with from_pretrained, keyed off the same model name string.

questions.q: What is an 'auto class' like AutoTokenizer or AutoModel?
options: A class that automatically trains a new model from scratch
A class that reads the model's config from the Hub and automatically picks the correct underlying architecture class
A class only usable with OpenAI models
A deprecated feature no longer recommended
questions.explain: Auto classes inspect the model's configuration and instantiate the right specific class, so the same from_pretrained call works across many different model architectures.

questions.q: What three groups of files does `from_pretrained` typically download from a model's Hub repository?
options: A video tutorial, a README, and a license file only
Only the weights file, nothing else
A Docker image and a requirements.txt
config.json (architecture), a weights file (trained parameters), and the tokenizer's files
questions.explain: The lesson's screenshot of a real model's Files tab showed exactly this: config.json, a weights file like pytorch_model.bin, and the tokenizer's vocabulary/config files.

questions.q: Why does the lesson recommend checking a model's own Hub page (downloads, usage by Spaces) before loading its name in code?
options: Because a model name is just a string, and from_pretrained will try to download a typo or illegitimate name just as readily as a well-established one
Because from_pretrained requires manual approval for every model
Because checking download counts is required by Hugging Face's terms of service
Because pipeline() cannot be used without it
questions.explain: from_pretrained doesn't validate that a name is a 'real' or trustworthy model — real download counts and Spaces usage are a practical, checkable sanity signal before relying on one.

questions.q: Why is the second call to `from_pretrained` for the same model much faster than the first?
options: Because the model automatically gets smaller after the first use
It isn't — every call re-downloads the files
Because the files were already downloaded and cached locally (by default in ~/.cache/huggingface/hub), so later calls read from disk instead of the network
Because the second call uses a different, faster model
questions.explain: transformers caches downloaded model files locally after the first from_pretrained call, so subsequent loads of the same model read from the local cache instead of re-downloading.
